question: Will Ituri province report at least 10 more new confirmed Ebola cases than Nord-Kivu province for 26 November 2026?

calls.reasoning: Daily Table 1 splits for 3,5-11 Nov 2026 show Ituri-minus-Nord-Kivu gaps of -13,-4,+23,+12,+17,+13,+20,-4: >=10 on 5 of 8 days. Cumulative-total changes from 11 to 14 Nov imply roughly +12/day (Ituri +93, NK +58), but revisions inflate these. Nord-Kivu's share of new cases is trending up (32.9% in SitRep 178, 49.4% on 11 Nov), which argues for a narrower gap by 26 Nov. With a mean gap around +9 to +12 and a day-to-day SD of about 13, the threshold sits near the median, so slightly under 50%. No human market matches; Polymarket's only related contract is 'WHO calls Ebola a pandemic' (~1.3%), which is irrelevant.
calls.dossier:
- Resolves off Table 1 of INSP SitRep for reporting date 26 Nov 2026 (expected N°196, published 27 Nov): Ituri daily new confirmed minus Nord-Kivu daily new confirmed >=10 -> Yes. It uses the daily figure attributed to that date, not the change in cumulative totals.
- Event window: one reporting day, 26 Nov 2026. As of 17 Nov, 9 days remain before that date.
- Daily splits, Ituri vs NK (INSP via question background and outbreaknewstoday, Nov 2026): 3 Nov 23 vs 36; 5 Nov 28 vs 32; 6 Nov 47 vs 24; 7 Nov 24 vs 12; 8 Nov 40 vs 23; 9 Nov 30 vs 17; 10 Nov 44 vs 24; 11 Nov 37 vs 41. Gaps: -13,-4,+23,+12,+17,+13,+20,-4. Gap >=10 on 5 of 8 days; gap <=9 on 3 of 8.
- National totals (ebola-tracker archive): N°181 (11 Nov) 11,197; N°182 (12 Nov) 11,254 (+57); N°183 (13 Nov) 11,316 (+62); N°184 (14 Nov) 11,376 (+60). Weekly average about 65/day as of 14 Nov.
- Cumulative by province: Ituri 7,765 (11 Nov) -> 7,858 (14 Nov), +93; NK 2,802 -> 2,860, +58. The implied average gap of about +12/day over 12-14 Nov includes retrospective revisions.
- Share of new cases: SitRep N°178 had Ituri 57.1% and NK 32.9%; on 11 Nov it was Ituri 44.6% and NK 49.4% (outbreaknewstoday). WHO DON (6 Nov): in the 21 days to 3 Nov, Ituri 710 and NK 640 of 1,463.
- NK hotspots: Beni, Katwa, Butembo, plus a new Mutwanga cluster. Ituri: Bunia (19 new on 10 Nov) and Mandima.
- No new health zones affected 11-14 Nov (68 zones, 8 provinces).
- Searched but could not get: the 12-16 Nov daily province splits from Table 1 (PDFs were not readable in this run).
- Markets: no market on province splits. The only related one is Polymarket 'WHO calls Ebola a pandemic in 2026'.

calls.reasoning: In the 8 days with a province split (3-11 Nov), Ituri led by 10 or more on 5. The gap ranged from NK+13 to Ituri+23 and averaged about Ituri+8, with a daily SD of about 13. Province totals for 11-14 Nov rose 93 in Ituri and 58 in Nord-Kivu, about +12/day for Ituri, but that includes back-dated revisions. Nord-Kivu's share of new notifications is rising (government, 10 Nov) and Radio Okapi reports falling cases in several Ituri zones (16 Nov), so the gap should narrow by 26 Nov. The forecast sits near a coin flip, shaded down. No human market found.

calls.reasoning: Daily Ituri-minus-Nord-Kivu gaps 3,5-11 Nov: -13,-4,+23,+12,+17,+13,+20,-4 (>=10 on 5/8; mean ~+8, SD ~13). Cumulative deltas 11-14 Nov imply ~+12/day for Ituri but include retrospective revisions. Nord-Kivu's share of new notifications is rising (32.9% -> 49.4%), officials call it the emerging main focus, and Radio Okapi (16 Nov) reports declining Ituri zone counts. Projected gap on 26 Nov ~+7 with SD ~13, so P(gap>=10) is about 42%. No human market found.
calls.reconciliation: All three runs share the same facts: the 3-11 Nov daily splits, the 11-14 Nov cumulative deltas (Ituri +93, NK +58), WHO DON 21-day figures (710 vs 640), the rising Nord-Kivu share, and Radio Okapi's report of Ituri declines. No factual conflicts. Unresolved fact: the 12-16 Nov daily splits, which no run could read and which I cannot retrieve without web access. The disagreement is judgment: how far the gap narrows by 26 Nov. Weighing the recent strong Ituri leads (6-10 Nov) and the cumulative-delta signal against the downward trend indicators, I take a projected gap of ~+7, SD ~13, giving ~42%.
